data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's gross claims outstanding at the start of the year were GBP 151.6m. Analysis of the claims development triangle shows a small net favourable prior-year development across the older underwriting years (primarily releases on 2017 more than offsetting some adverse development on 2018), resulting in an overall small release of approximately GBP 1.6m. The movement reflects normal claims development patterns and reserve re-estimation, with prior large weather events (e.g. Typhoons Hagibis, Faxai and Jebi) noted in the report as influencing currency and reinsurance recoveries.
raw_causal_phrases: The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.
The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit textual sentence quantifying a GROSS prior-year movement was located. The prior year development figure was calculated from the gross claims development table (claims triangle) which is presented in thousands. The Part VII reinsurance/transfer activity noted in the report (transfer of EEA policies to Lloyd's Brussels) may distort some comparative movements for EEA-related business; no gross prior-year movement note (Insurance liabilities column) was found to use directly, so the triangle was used as the primary source.
